scope: C4 delivery core only; C5 route and live/provider proof excluded

findings.title: Concurrent delivery calls can create duplicate Checks or PRs
findings.reason: The SQL governor lock ends after createDeliveryIntent. Two callers can both read pending and an empty Check list, then both POST a Check. They can similarly both list no PR and POST a PR. The durable row does not claim either external attempt before the write, and the later identity conflict only occurs after duplicates may exist.
findings.repair: Persist an exclusive, expiring per-intent external-attempt claim/phase before each create, with a stable operation identity. A concurrent caller must observe in-flight/UNKNOWN and reconcile, never enter the same create window. Exercise two independent SQL connections and controlled overlapping calls.

findings.title: An ambiguous Check write before PR creation cannot be recovered to progress
findings.reason: Any Check POST timeout marks the whole intent unknown. The only unknown recovery demands exactly one successful Check and one draft PR, even though no PR was attempted. Thus a normal interrupted Check cannot advance, and the packet's restart-after-each-effect requirement fails.
findings.repair: Record which external effect was attempted and reconcile that phase independently. After one exact Check is found, durably transition to check_created and allow the PR phase. If no match after an ambiguous attempt, remain UNKNOWN for operator resolution; do not blindly retry.

findings.title: Successful Check response is accepted without an independent readback
findings.reason: After POST, the code validates the returned object and remote branch but does not GET/list the created Check before persisting check_created. A response from an intermediary or stale/faulty provider can make a non-observed Check count as delivered.
findings.repair: List Checks after POST and require exactly one matching ID, SHA, name, external ID, successful conclusion, and trusted App identity before storing check_created. Treat failed or ambiguous readback as UNKNOWN.

findings.title: Check readback does not verify the issuing GitHub App
findings.reason: The adapter strips Check app metadata. A Check with the same SHA/name/external ID from another App could be adopted or accepted during reconciliation. The check external ID is predictable from mission, slice, epoch, and SHA.
findings.repair: Return and validate check_run.app.id against configured appId on both create response and list readback. Retain source identity with the observed Check ID.

findings.title: Closed draft PR can satisfy completed delivery replay
findings.reason: PR list includes state=all, but the returned contract omits state and merged status. A closed draft PR with matching head/base and draft=true can pass assertPr and be returned as pr_created.
findings.repair: Carry PR state/merged status through list and get. Require an open unmerged draft PR at creation, reconciliation, and replay.

additionalBoundaries: The packet requires secure upload of the exact local commit or independently verified already-uploaded branch. This core only implements the latter; report remote upload as an explicit prerequisite, not a delivery capability.
C5 owner-session route is absent by planned file ownership. No claim of end-to-end acceptance can follow from this review.

The three focused tests do not cover crash/restart phase recovery, concurrency, App identity, or closed PR. Completion handoff itself records full suite, real PostgreSQL recovery, independent final review, and live App/R2 proof as unrun.
reviewLimit: No code mutation, external call, test run, or live acceptance claim was made.
